insights.headline: Goldman Sachs pushes Fed hike call to December as soft PCE lifts gold near $4,192; NFP on Friday is next
insights.summary: Gold steadied at $4,191.90 and silver at $60.97 on Thursday after August PCE printed 3.4% vs 3.7% expected, prompting Goldman Sachs to push its next-hike call to December; October-hike odds fell to 38% from 71% a week ago. Multi-decade-high yields and a firm dollar still cap bullion, with Friday's payrolls next. Domestic 99.9% gold rose ₹700 to ₹1.49 lakh/10g on Sept 30 while silver held at ₹2.32 lakh/kg; ETF holdings rose five days straight. Four SGB tranches face RBI premature redemption in October — first deadline Oct 5, and the exemption is maturity-only from FY27.
points: August PCE at 3.4% vs 3.7% expected drove Goldman Sachs to delay its next-hike call to December; CME FedWatch shows 38% October-hike odds vs 71% a week ago.
Gold steadied at $4,191.90 and silver at $60.97 after September's correction; the metal is ~10% above year-ago levels, with elevated yields still capping gains.
Friday's US nonfarm payrolls (consensus 90,000 jobs, unemployment 4.1%) is the next macro catalyst; the Fed meets on October 28.
Domestic gold rose ₹700 to ₹1.49 lakh/10g on Sept 30; festive/wedding-season demand is being watched as prices stabilise.
Four SGB tranches face RBI premature redemption in October; request deadlines run Oct 5–21, and the FY27 rule change makes the exemption maturity-only.

items.title: Goldman Sachs pushes Fed rate hike forecast to December
items.summary: Goldman Sachs pushed its next-hike call to December after August PCE inflation printed 3.4% versus 3.7% expected, Reuters reports. The brokerage had forecast a 25bp October hike. "We see a strong chance the FOMC will ultimately conclude additional rate hikes are unnecessary," it said. October-hike odds fell to 38% from 71% a week ago, per CME FedWatch. Friday's US nonfarm payrolls report is next.

items.title: Gold, silver prices today: What investors should watch after September correction
items.summary: Gold was steady on October 1 while silver gained as investors weighed US rates, yields and the dollar, CNBC TV18 reports. COMEX gold traded at $4,191.90 (+0.12%) and silver at $60.965 (+0.66%); domestic 99.9% gold rose ₹700 to ₹1.49 lakh/10g with silver flat at ₹2.32 lakh/kg. Elevated yields cap bullion while ETF holdings rose five days straight; the Oct 2 US jobs report is next.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD holds above $61.00 amid easing Fed rate hike expectations
items.summary: Silver regained ground to around $60.90 in Asian hours Thursday as softer US inflation eased Fed-hike bets, FXStreet reports. October-hike odds fell to 38% from nearly 51% pre-PCE, per CME FedWatch; annual PCE eased to 3.4% vs 3.7% expected. Gains face caps from elevated oil and yields (10-yr ~5.298%, 30-yr ~5.633%); TD Securities still expects an October hike but allows a more gradual path.

items.title: 10-year Treasury yield rises to new 24-year high, posts largest quarterly gain since 1994
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.304% on Wednesday, its highest since May 2002, after US Q2 GDP was revised up to 2.2% and August PCE inflation held at 3.4%. The 30-year touched about 5.65%, and the 10-year posted its largest quarterly gain since 1994 — nearly 0.9 points. Traders now see only about a 37% chance of an October Fed hike.

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Gower sees gold back above $5,000 in H2 2027; silver's run to $120 driven by more than hype
items.summary: Morgan Stanley's Amy Gower told CNBC she expects gold to trade back above $5,000 an ounce within a year, citing strong ETF and central-bank demand despite 20-year-high long-dated yields and dollar strength. She said silver's surge to $120 was driven by fundamentals rather than hype, and pointed to China's record gold imports and Golden Week buying as support.

items.title: Yields, dollar hold key to gold, silver trajectory in H2FY27: Apurva Seth
items.summary: SAMCO Securities' Apurva Sheth says US real yields, the dollar and central-bank policy expectations will decide whether gold's correction deepens or becomes the launch pad for the next leg higher. Gold has fallen about 11% since April to the $4,100–$4,200 zone from record highs above $5,600; he sees a technically plausible recovery toward $4,600 if real yields fall.

items.title: Rupee to fall more, yield curve to shift higher in H2FY27: Gaura Sengupta
items.summary: IDFC First Bank chief economist Gaura Sengupta expects the rupee to depreciate further in H2FY27 as RBI intervention turns more cautious now that the FCNR(B) window has closed — the $133 billion mobilised is borrowed money to be repaid in three years. Persistent dollar strength and high US yields keep foreign capital away, pushing the G-sec yield curve higher.

items.title: Will festive season revive gold jewellery demand as prices remain 9% above last year?
items.summary: Gold jewellery demand may rise during India's festive and wedding season, but high prices could push buyers towards lighter designs, gold exchange and value-focused jewellery purchases.

items.title: High gold prices and steep taxes push more Indian buyers toward off-the-books cash deals
items.summary: Mint reports that soaring gold prices and the import duty hike to 15% (plus 3% GST) are driving more buyers into under-the-counter cash sales without invoices, where bulk buyers can save up to 6%. The shift toward the grey market ahead of the wedding season is an unintended consequence of the policy meant to curb bullion purchases and protect forex reserves.

items.title: SGB premature redemption October 2026: 4 tranches eligible for early exit
items.summary: RBI scheduled premature redemption for four SGB tranches — 2019-20 Series V and VI and 2020-21 Series I and VII, Livemint reports. Deadlines: Oct 5 (Series V, redeems Oct 15), Oct 9 (Series VII, Oct 19), Oct 19 (Series I, Oct 28), Oct 21 (Series VI, Oct 30). Value uses IBJA's 3-day 999-gold average. From FY27 the capital-gains exemption applies only if held to maturity, so early exit may be taxed.
